- Provide an estimated time-to-complete and a deletion confirmation artifact we can retain for our records (timestamp + operator id).

Subject: Re: Request to remove single conversation from telemetry (AST-DEL-72)

Elena —

Thanks for the heads up and for the attachment. We can handle targeted removals, but I need to confirm a couple of operational details before we proceed:

1) Scope: when you say "conversation" can you confirm whether this is a single Redwood-generated conversation id (AST-DEL-72-THREAD) or multiple linked messages across threads? We can remove at the conversation id level quickly; cross-thread correlations require more time.

2) Approval: I need explicit authorization from a customer security lead (you are fine) plus a signed request on company letterhead for audit (this is standard for EU-residency destructive actions). A simple signed PDF is OK.

3) Evidence artifact: we will provide a deletion record (operator id, UTC timestamp, target ids removed, checksum) and a short CSV as an attachment. That will be stored in our compliance ledger for 6 months per the current contract. If you require longer retention of the proof, tell me and we can route through an enterprise retention addendum.

Operational ETA: once we have the signed authorization, SOC/Privacy ops will triage and attempt removal from EU stores within 48 hours. If the conversation surfaces in cached indexes or warm KV caches, we may need up to 5 business days to fully propagate the deletion and produce the confirmation artifact.

Next steps: please reply with a signed authorization PDF and confirm that single conversation id = AST-DEL-72-THREAD. If you prefer, I can introduce Marissa (Privacy Ops) to coordinate execution.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
